conditions.unmeasured: figures downstream of a constant nobody has measured are absent rather than estimated
conditions.what_an_interval_here_is: a statement about this model's declared inputs, and nothing about whether the model has the right structure (ch14, ch19)

produced_by.sampler: sizing.mc — inverse transform, Iman-Conover rank correlation

correlations.because: A platform that is growing is a platform that is being changed, and labels arrive with changes. Treating the two as independent makes the metrics interval narrower than the estate warrants — ch14 measures by how much.

Weak and positive: busier services tend to be the chattier ones. Small enough to be worth including as an example of a correlation that barely matters, which is a useful thing for a reader to see beside one that does.

A busier platform is one more people are watching. Moderate rather than strong: most query load comes from alert rules and dashboards on timers, which do not care how busy anything is — right up until an incident, when they all fire at once and nobody is looking at the model.

summary.description:
The book's second model, and the counterweight to the web service. Three multiplicative chains hang off the same few roots, so they are correlated whether or not anybody says so; label cardinality is a product of uncertain counts and therefore dominates everything downstream of it; the control knobs are sampling and retention rather than money; and there are three separate outputs with three separate ceilings, which no single number can summarise.
It also has a hole in it. Spans per request is a property of somebody's instrumented application, not of any corpus or any machine, so this repository cannot measure it — and the whole traces chain is therefore shown as unmeasured rather than filled in with a plausible number. That is not a gap waiting to be tidied up. It is what an honest sizing model looks like before the measurement is taken, and it is on a published page for exactly that reason.

provenance.source: ch04 — telemetry grows faster than the traffic it describes, because teams add instrumentation as well as load. Lognormal like any growth rate — it compounds and cannot go negative — and wider than the web service's for the same reason its median is higher

base_metrics_per_host.label: metric names per host
base_metrics_per_host.note: No band: scrape one host and list them. The uncertainty in this chain is what the labels multiply that list by, and label_cardinality carries it.

provenance.source: distinct metric names exposed per host, before labels
the sizing decision for the ingest tier

collector_throughput_measured.label: collector throughput per core, measured
collector_throughput_measured.note: The same quantity as the node above, taken rather than quoted. It needs the reference machine (`rig`) and nobody has run it, so the ceiling built on it is absent while the ceiling built on the vendor's claim is not. This node sits beside `collector_throughput_quoted` in ch03, so the pipeline capacity each gives can be compared.

collector_throughput_quoted.label: collector throughput quoted
collector_throughput_quoted.note: No band, and giving a quote one would be inventing a range nobody quoted. A vendor states a single number; the spread belongs to the measurement, and collector_throughput_measured below carries it with a standard error.

provenance.source: throughput per core as documented by the collector. Unverified here, and marked as a claim in every figure it appears in
the planning horizon for this platform

hosts.label: hosts
hosts.note: No band: an estate is a thing you can count, and this one has been counted. What it does next is growth_factor's business, not this node's.

provenance.source: the estate's host count as stated by its operators

known_ingest.label: ingest, metrics and logs only
known_ingest.note: Metrics plus logs, and deliberately *not* the total. It is a lower bound with a whole chain missing from it, and ch19 is about exactly this shape of error: a number that is correct arithmetic over an incomplete structure looks identical to a number that is right.

known_storage_cost.label: retention cost, metrics and logs only

label_cardinality.label: label cardinality
label_cardinality.note: A product of uncertain counts, which is why it is lognormal-ish whether or not anybody chose that. One of its inputs, the accidental label, leads the tornado for every metrics figure in this model. Its band is wider than any one count's, narrower than their widths multiplied, because the three counts rarely sit at their high ends together. No amount of care about the other inputs narrows it.

label_values_accidental.label: accidental label values
label_values_accidental.note: One plus the extra values: the number of values the accidental label takes. That is the factor it multiplies the series count by, and it is never below one.

label_values_accidental_extra.label: extra accidental label values
label_values_accidental_extra.note: The label nobody planned: a pod name under a rolling deploy, a customer id added during an incident, a version string. Counted from the second value, because a label with one value multiplies the series count by one, so this input can only add series, never take any away. Lognormal and wide, because the failure mode is multiplicative: whatever the label is, it multiplies every series that carries it, and the band has to span from usually a little to occasionally catastrophic.

provenance.source: ch08 — the cardinality explosion, as a band rather than as a warning. Lognormal because this one has no ceiling: a label carrying a user id multiplies the series count by a number nobody chose, and a triangular would assert a maximum that does not exist. Counted from the second value, so the factor it feeds is never below one.
distinct routes appearing as a label value. Triangular because somebody could go and count them this afternoon; the maximum is the routes that exist today, and a new service adds to it
distinct status classes kept as a label. Triangular, and the one input in this model whose bounds are genuinely hard: a request cannot carry a status the code does not emit
application log lines emitted per request served. Triangular, from reading a sample of the logs — and the maximum is the part to distrust, because a debug flag left on in production is outside it
a control knob (ch12): drop and aggregation rules

measured.corpus: bench.measure.log_lines — JSON service logs, five templates, six services, 128-bit trace ids, seeds 0-7

provenance.source: a control knob (ch12)
a control knob (ch12)

measured.corpus: bench.measure.metric_samples — 400 series x 500 points, 15/30/60s scrape intervals with occasional jitter, lognormal random-walk values, seeds 0-7
measured.stack: this repository's encoder, not any product's

one_sample_per_series.label: one sample per series
one_sample_per_series.note: one scrape takes one sample from one series. A rate is a count over a duration, and the count needs a unit before the division means anything

provenance.source: definition

one_year.label: one year
one_year.note: as in the web service model: an exponent has to be a pure number

provenance.source: definition
dashboards, alert rules and people, at the busy hour. Triangular because two of those three are countable and the third is not
the sizing decision for the query tier

query_scan_rate_quoted.label: query scan rate quoted
query_scan_rate_quoted.note: No band, for the same reason as the collector's quoted throughput: a quote is one number, and widening it here would put a range in the vendor's mouth. Nobody has measured this one, so nothing in this model disputes it yet.

provenance.source: series scanned per second per query node, quoted

ceiling.because: Queueing again, and the tier where a breach is most visible: a dashboard that times out during an incident is the failure people remember. Cardinality feeds this and the ingest ceiling by different routes, so a single accidental label breaks both at once.

A queueing ceiling, not a capacity one (ch06), so the margin is large: a pipeline at 80% of quoted throughput has a queue in front of it, and a queue in front of an ingest pipeline is dropped telemetry exactly when something is going wrong. Understated twice over — the numerator excludes traces and the denominator is a vendor's claim.

provenance.source: ch04 — the busy hour across the estate, not the daily mean. Triangular: a minimum, a likely and a maximum is the whole of what a dashboard gives you, and the maximum is the busiest hour anybody has looked at rather than the busiest one there will be
a control knob (ch12): doubling it halves the metrics chain and loses resolution that cannot be recovered afterwards

series_per_query.label: series per query
series_per_query.note: The same cardinality node that drives the metrics ingest chain drives this one too, by a different route: a label that multiplies the series a scrape produces also multiplies the series a query has to walk past to ignore. That is why one accidental label breaks two ceilings at once, and why turning down scrape interval and retention — which fix the first — does nothing at all for the second (ch12).

provenance.source: how many distinct metric-name-and-host combinations one dashboard panel or alert rule covers, before any label expansion. Triangular, and wide: dashboards differ from each other more than anything else in this model does

spans_per_request.label: spans per request
spans_per_request.note: Not measurable from anything in this repository. It is a property of one instrumented application at one version, so it belongs to the `estate` target — an observation somebody takes of a system they run, disclosed rather than verified (ch03). Until somebody takes it, every figure below is absent rather than estimated.

provenance.source: all-in cost of a usable TB-month on this tier. Lognormal because it is a price — and carried across by hand from whichever storage tier's unit economics somebody had to hand, rather than by sampling, which is the seam ch18 is about

ceiling.because: Capacity, with a rebuild reserve (ch11) — and again a lower bound, because the traces chain is not in the numerator. A verdict of `ok` here means "ok, ignoring traces", which is a different claim and one the reader should be made to notice.

provenance.source: the sizing decision for the retention tier
a control knob (ch12), and the one with the widest range: head sampling at 1% and at 100% are two different platforms
a control knob (ch12)

measured.corpus: bench.measure.trace_spans — spans with 2-14 attributes drawn from a ten-key vocabulary, 128-bit trace ids, seeds 0-7

provenance.source: usable capacity per storage node after replication

scenario.because: The platform as declared: 30-second scrapes, 400-day metric retention, 30-day logs, 5% trace sampling. Every figure the book quotes for this model comes from here unless it says otherwise.
